questions.q: Trace the development of modern Indian art in the twentieth century.
answer: In the twentieth century, Indian art moved beyond the revivalism of the Bengal School towards a modern art that combined global techniques with Indian roots.

answer.text: Early modernists broke new ground. Rabindranath Tagore painted spontaneous, expressive works, while Amrita Sher-Gil blended European technique with sensitive portrayals of Indian village life and women. Jamini Roy turned to the bold, flat forms of Bengal folk and Kalighat art, and Nandalal Bose linked tradition with modern expression.

In 1947, the Progressive Artists' Group was founded in Bombay by artists such as F.N. Souza, S.H. Raza and M.F. Husain. They embraced modern styles like Cubism and abstraction while drawing on Indian themes, and gave Indian art an international presence.
In sculpture, Ramkinkar Baij pioneered a modern approach at Santiniketan.

answer: Thus modern Indian art grew varied and confident, uniting global modernism with Indian identity.
